Where it began

Mayank Agarwal was born in Bangalore on 16 February 1991. He went to Bishop Cotton Boys' School and then Jain University, where his teammates included K. L. Rahul and Karun Nair.

He first made people notice in age-group cricket. He was India's leading run-getter at the 2010 Under-19 World Cup, and that same year the Karnataka Premier League named him its player of the series.

The player

The 2017–18 season changed everything. He made 304 not out against Maharashtra, the 50th triple-hundred in Indian first-class cricket, and finished with 1,160 runs in the Ranji Trophy and 2,141 across all formats, the most by anyone in an Indian domestic season.

The Test call came in Australia. On debut at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 26 December 2018 he made seventy-six, the best by an Indian on Test debut in that country. Within a year he had made 215 against South Africa and 243 against Bangladesh at Indore. He played 21 Tests between 2018 and 2022, scoring 1,488 runs at 41.33 with 4 hundreds.

What made him special

Agarwal had a rare knack of turning a hundred into something much bigger. Those two double-centuries came in only 12 innings, a quicker start than Don Bradman managed. Later, against New Zealand, he marked his return to the side with 150 and 62 and the player of the match award.

His one-day international chances came mostly as a late call-up to cover for others, so it was in Test cricket that India saw the best of him.

Away from the middle

He became a leader in the domestic game, captaining Karnataka and, in 2022, the Punjab Kings in the IPL. For the Kings he had made a 106 off 50 balls in 2020. He won the Madhavrao Scindia Award in 2018 as the leading run-scorer in the Ranji Trophy, and in August 2026 Durham signed him for the rest of that County Championship season.

And finally

The first time he led Punjab Kings, in 2021, he made 99 not out. He was named player of the match all the same, which seems a fair price for the missing run.
